root_cause.text: In md/raid10, the NOWAIT I/O error path during a raised barrier incorrectly called `raid_end_bio_io()` on an `r10bio` that had never incremented `conf->nr_pending`, causing `allow_barrier()` to unconditionally decrement `nr_pending`, underflow it, and deadlock resync/barrier handling.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states NOWAIT requests “do not increment nr_pending in wait_barrier()” but `raid_end_bio_io()` “eventually calls allow_barrier() and it will unconditionally do an atomic_dec_and_test(&conf->nr_pending),” and the fix replaces `raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio)` with `free_r10bio(r10_bio)` in both `raid10_read_request()` and `raid10_write_request()` when `regular_request_wait()` fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the raid10 read-request wait-failure path to free the r10bio directly instead of ending it as completed I/O.
intent_record.what: In raid10_read_request(), the failure path after regular_request_wait(mddev, conf, bio, r10_bio->sectors) returns false was changed from calling raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio) to calling free_r10bio(r10_bio), with the early return kept unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the read request cannot proceed because regular_request_wait() fails, the code now directly frees the raid10 bio structure instead of completing it through the normal I/O end handler. This avoids treating the request as a completed I/O in that path and ensures the object is cleaned up using the appropriate failure-handling routine.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the raid10 write-request wait-failure path to free the r10_bio directly instead of incorrectly ending bio I/O.
intent_record.what: In raid10_write_request(), the failure path after regular_request_wait(mddev, conf, bio, sectors) returns false was changed from calling raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio) to calling free_r10bio(r10_bio), with the early return left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the write request cannot proceed because regular_request_wait() fails, the code now directly frees the r10_bio structure instead of completing it through the normal bio-I/O end path. This avoids invoking completion handling for a request that was not actually issued and ensures the object is cleaned up using the appropriate failure-path teardown.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the raid10 read-request wait-failure path to free the r10bio directly instead of ending it as completed I/O.
Fix the raid10 write-request wait-failure path to free the r10_bio directly instead of incorrectly ending bio I/O.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the NOWAIT/read wait-failure error path in raid10 by freeing the r10bio instead of calling the normal I/O completion path. That matches the root cause where raid_end_bio_io() was incorrectly called on an r10bio that never incremented nr_pending, leading to allow_barrier() underflow and deadlock.

The change directly fixes the raid10 NOWAIT/write wait-failure path by avoiding raid_end_bio_io() on an r10bio that never raised nr_pending, which matches the root cause of the nr_pending underflow and barrier/resync deadlock.

candidates.rationale: On the regular_request_wait() failure path, this treats the r10bio as if normal I/O completion bookkeeping had occurred. Per the root cause, conf->nr_pending was never incremented for this NOWAIT/barrier-failed request, so raid_end_bio_io() ultimately causes allow_barrier() to decrement nr_pending anyway, leading to underflow and barrier/resync deadlock.

This identical call in the write-request wait-failure path incorrectly runs completed-I/O cleanup on an r10_bio that never acquired the pending-count reference. That mismatched lifecycle triggers an unconditional nr_pending decrement in allow_barrier(), causing underflow and deadlock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This NOWAIT/barrier wait-failure path incorrectly invokes normal I/O completion handling on an r10_bio that never incremented conf->nr_pending. That causes allow_barrier() to unconditionally decrement nr_pending, leading to underflow and barrier/resync deadlock.

Author: Nigel Croxon <ncroxon@redhat.com>
Date:   Thu Jul 3 11:23:04 2025 -0400

    raid10: cleanup memleak at raid10_make_request
    
    If raid10_read_request or raid10_write_request registers a new
    request and the REQ_NOWAIT flag is set, the code does not
    free the malloc from the mempool.
    
    unreferenced object 0xffff8884802c3200 (size 192):
       comm "fio", pid 9197, jiffies 4298078271
       hex dump (first 32 bytes):
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact NOWAIT error-path change in the relevant functions. In both `raid10_read_request()` and `raid10_write_request()`, this commit adds: `if (!regular_request_wait(mddev, conf, bio, ...)) { raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio); return; }`. The root cause says the bug occurs when the NOWAIT path during a raised barrier calls `raid_end_bio_io()` on an `r10bio` that never incremented `conf->nr_pending`, causing `allow_barrier()` to decrement it incorrectly. The added call to `raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio)` is exactly that vulnerable construct on the failure path of `regular_request_wait(...)`, i.e. the path where the request did not successfully wait/register and thus did not obtain the pending/barrier accounting. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present in this commit. Since the fix would be to avoid calling `raid_end_bio_io()` on this path (and instead only free the allocation without touching pending/barrier accounting), this commit does not contain the fix.

    This adds nowait support to the RAID10 driver. Very similar to

    for situations where it could wait for eg:
    
      - Waiting for the barrier,
      - Reshape operation,
      - Discard operation.
    
    wait_barrier() and regular_request_wait() f
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant barrier/pending logic clearly. In `wait_barrier(struct r10conf *conf, bool nowait)`, when `conf->barrier` is set and `nowait` is true, the new code does `ret = false` and skips waiting, and then only does `atomic_inc(&conf->nr_pending);` when `ret` is true: `if (ret) atomic_inc(&conf->nr_pending);`. So in the NOWAIT/barrier case, no pending reference is taken. However, callers newly return early on NOWAIT with `bio_wouldblock_error(bio); return false;` in `regular_request_wait()`, and `raid10_read_request()` / `raid10_write_request()` return immediately when that happens. The root-cause vulnerability is specifically that the NOWAIT error path later called `raid_end_bio_io()` on an `r10bio` that never incremented `conf->nr_pending`, causing `allow_barrier()` to decrement unconditionally and underflow. This commit introduces the prerequisite vulnerable construct: `wait_barrier()` can now return without incrementing `nr_pending` in the NOWAIT case, but there is no corresponding protection in this shown code to prevent the end-I/O path from calling `allow_barrier()`/`raid_end_bio_io()` only when a pending ref was actually acquired. Thus the vulnerable condition is present, and the fix is not present in this function set.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided diff is sufficient because it shows the exact barrier/pending handling around the split-bio path that caused the hang. In both affected functions, the split path now does `allow_barrier(conf);` before `generic_make_request(bio);` and then `wait_barrier(conf);` afterward. Specifically, in `raid10_read_request()` the added lines are `allow_barrier(conf);` before `generic_make_request(bio);` and `wait_barrier(conf);` after it; the same pattern is added in `raid10_write_request()`. This matches the commit message's fix description: 'we need to call allow_barrier to decrease nr_pending before generic_make_request ... and wait_barrier is called again'. Therefore, this commit version already contains the corrective handling for barrier/nr_pending accounting in the split-I/O path, so the vulnerable construct is not present here.
